MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
J  SPETEMBER 23, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 PM.

  MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 6:33pm.

  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins; and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda
  Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director; Maureen Tamuri, Interim Planning
  Director; Susan Duenas, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBouX, Public Works Director;
  Parker Davis, Media Technician; and Jason Lawrence, Deputy City Clerk

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Channing Frykman led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  September 13, 2024, with the amended agenda posted on September 20, 2024.

  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a
  motion to approve the agenda, hearing Item No. 6.A. before Item No. 4.A. The
  motion carried unanimously.

  ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

  ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Mayor Stewart discussed the purpose of public comment and reminded the public
  L  to limit their comments to items on the agenda or issues within the City Council’s
  subject matter jurisdiction.

  Anne Payne stated she lived in Serra Canyon along Malibu Creek. She discussed
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 23, 2024
  Page 2 of 10

  how the creek had changed since the 19803. She discussed a State Parks grant to
  remove invasive plants. She discussed a letter from an expert on Malibu Creek to
  State Parks explaining damage to the creek.

  Shelly Crema discussed how Malibu Creek needed maintenance. She discussed
  flooding and erosion on her property.

  Norm Haynie discussed a candidate forum he attended. He discussed the
  communications tower at Santa Monica College Malibu Campus and stated the
  tower could be moved behind the school building.

  Ron discussed code enforcement. He stated Malibu Township Council members
  reported code enforcement violations on behalf of John Mazza and discussed Mr.
  Mazza’s access to information at the City as a Planning Commissioner. He
  discussed how Code Enforcement staff handled complaints and entered private
  properties. He stated Code Enforcement staff did not have the right to enter private
  property without a court order.

  Ari discussed Facebook posts made by Councilmember Silverstein in 2020.

  Ann Doneen discussed Malibu Township Council (MTC) and its history before the
  City was incorporated.

  Jo Drummond stated she had verified her residency with City staff. She discussed
  accusations against her, MTC, Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember
  Uhring, and John Mazza. She stated she had reported Councilmember Grisanti to
  the FPPC for organizing these attacks.

  Rosemarie Ihde was unavailable at the time of the hearing.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary announced that the City’s Human Resources team would
  attend the Los Angeles career fair. He announced that the school district separation
  subcommittees had come to an agreement on a school district separation package
  and the draft agreements were now available for public review. He stated once the
  agreements were approved by both entities in October, the Los Angeles County
  Office of Education (LACOE) Board would hold public hearings in Malibu and
  Santa Monica on the separation petition. He stated the City was waiting on an
  update from the Governor’s Office on the speed camera bill (SB 1297). He stated
  staff had submitted comments to the California Coastal Commission (CCC)
  regarding the public access project at Lechuza Beach. He stated CCC took
  jurisdiction over the matter and approved the restroom. He stated the City held the
  fifth annual Safety and Preparedness Fair and it was well attended. He discussed
  the earthquake on September 12, 2024. He stated the Disaster Council met on
  September l2, 2024 to review the City’s disaster plan, which would be brought to
  Council for final approval. He discussed the coastal cleanup event last weekend
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 23, 2024
  Page 3 of 10

  with California Wildlife Center and Heal the Bay at Nicholas Canyon. He
  announced the Topanga Lagoon Restoration Project restoration plan had been
  approved by State Parks. He stated he attended the quarterly PCH Task Force
  meeting and a Las Virgenes-Malibu Council of Governments meeting. He stated
  the City held a City COuncil Candidates information meeting on September 12,
  2024. He discussed the September 18, 2024 Special meeting and stated the updated
  workplan would be coming back for adoption. He stated the City held two
  leadership and good govemance workshop for Councilmembers and
  Commissioners. He announced that the next City Council meeting would be on
  October 14, 2024 and would begin at 5:30 p.m. with the new format.

  In response to Councilmember Grisanti, City Manager McClary stated staff could
  initiate a recruitment process for the Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization
  Commission and bring an item back to Council to fill the vacancies.

  In response to Councilmember Grisanti, City Clerk Pettijohn stated that each
  Councilmember would appoint one commissioner to Mobilehome Park Rent
  Stabilization Commission.

  Councilmember Grisanti discussed the recent sale of the Point Dume Club
  Mobilehome Park.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins indicated support for filling the vacancies on the
  Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission.

  Councilmember Silverstein requested consensus to bring back an item to fill the
  vacancies on the Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission and suggested
  forming an Ad Hoc Committee to review the rent control ordinance.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item on the Mobilehome
  Park Rent Stabilization Commission and the Mobilehome Park Rent Control
  Regulations.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, discussed an
  arson incident on September 18, 2024 at Nicholas Canyon Beach. He discussed a
  burglary at Aviator Nation on September 19, r2024. He discussed a DUI arrest on
  September 19, 2024. He discussed an arrest he made on September 17, 2024. He
  stated staff had removed the unattached trailer near Corral Canyon. He discussed
  plans for a drone program. He stated Sheriff s Department staff attended the Safety
  and Preparedness Fair.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, Sergeant Soderlund discussed plans for the
  new drone.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 23, 2024
  Page 4 of 10
2

  Councilmember Silverstein asked Ms. Payne and Ms. Crema to clarify how the City
  can help them. He addressed Ron, and stated Councilmembers and Planning
  Commissioners did not have access to the City’s servers and had to request
  information from staff. He requested consensus to bring back an item on another
  Malibu Film Society series at City Hall.

  CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staffto bring back an item on a fllm series with
  the Malibu Film Society.
  ' City Manager McClary stated staff would look into the
  proposal and see how it can
  be worked into the staff schedule.

  Councilmember Silverstein addressed Ms. Drummond and stated he had not seen
  any evidence that Councilmember Grisanti was involved in the political attacks.
  He discussed the Facebook meme page he created during the COVID-19 pandemic.

  Councilmember Grisanti discussed the dam removal and Malibu Creek. He stated
  he volunteered at the Safety and Preparedness Fair. He stated he attended an
  interfaith breakfast at the Lost Hills Sheriff” s Station and had a tour of the real time
  crime center. He encouraged business owners and residents to register their
  cameras with the real time crime center. He stated he attended a Beaches and
  Harbors meeting regarding the beach nourishment project.

  City Manager McClary stated he would reach out to the State Parks Superintendent
  regarding Malibu Creek and an item could be scheduled for the City Council, if
  needed.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Ms. Payne stated the issues with Malibu
  Creek were within and outside City limits.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed plans for the dam removal and stated State Parks
  would need to take action. Councilmember Uhring requested a commendation be
  scheduled to recognize the 25th anniversary of the Malibu Farmers Market. He
  encouraged the public to complete the community lands survey before it closes.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins stated she attended the Safety and Preparedness Fair, the
  coastal cleanup event at Nicholas Canyon Beach, and a library speaker series event.
  She stated she had been contacted by parents interested in a pilot program for school
  security. She requested consensus to bring back an item.

  CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back a school safety item to
  discuss school resource officers

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins announced the next library speaker series event on
  September 30, 2024.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 23, 2024
  Page 5 of 10

  Mayor Stewart discussed the Malibu Creek issue. He discussed the Governor’s
  veto of Senator Stern’s SB 1509 and stated the City hoped the Govemor would
  approve SB 1297. He stated he attended the PCH Taskforce meeting with Mayor
  Pro Tem Riggins and stated he learned that encroachment permits were not required
  for law enforcement devices. He discussed the Lost Hills Sheriff‘s Station’s new
  real time crime system. He discussed Supervisor Horvath’s proposal to add tow-
  away parking signs on PCH near Sunset Mesa to address oversized vehicles long-
  term parking.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to discuss adding
  tow-away zones along Pacific Coast Highway.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Interim City Attomey Rusin stated
  parking signs can affect the intensity land use and the CCC’s interpretation was that
  signs require a coastal development permit.

  Sergeant Soderlund stated CCC wanted to be involved in any changes to coastal
  - s1gnage.

  Councilmember Grisanti discussed how long-term parked cars impacted access to
  the beach.

  Interim City Attomey Rusin confirmed that argument had been used in the City’s
  previous parking restriction applications.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Item Nos. 3.B.l 1., 3.B.13., and 3.B.14. were pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. 3.B.1 1., 3.B.13., and 3.B.14.
  The motion carried unanimously.

  A.  Previously Discussed Items

  B.  New Items

  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers

  Agreement for Annual Routine Street Maintenance Services

  Agreement for Citywide Tree Maintenance Services

10.  Agreement for Annual Street Sweeping Services

  15.  Professional Services Agreements for Contract Planning Services
  Recommended Action: 1) Authorize the Mayor to execute a professional

  16.  Amendment to Agreement with Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School

  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 1

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  11.  Professional Services Agreement for PCH Median Improvements —
  Paradise Cove and Zuma Beach
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute a Professional
  Services Agreement with Kimley Horn and Associates, Inc. for engineering
  design services for the PCH Median Improvements — Paradise Cove and
  Zuma Beach in the amount not to exceed $296,670.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Stewart moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded a motion to
  authorize the Mayor to execute a Professional Services Agreement with
  Kimley Hom and Associates, Inc. for engineering design services for the
  PCH Median Improvements — Paradise Cove and Zuma Beach in the
  amount not to exceed $296,670. The motion carried unanimously.

  13.  Amendment to Professional Services Agreement with Kimley Horn and
  Associates, Inc
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 5
  to the Professional Services Agreement with Kimley Hom and Associates,

  This proposed amendment includes additional engineering design service
